task.description: Diagnose GH #504 (ISS-0176, MAJOR): LUA-07's criterion 2 ('The manifest hash appears in the execution audit record') is unsatisfied. src/lua/ (manifest.zig, executor.zig) correctly produces manifest_hash on ScriptResult (criterion 1, already satisfied per ISS-0169 tranche 1) but nothing in the engine consumes it and writes it to the persisted execution audit record. This is a scope-boundary gap, not a defect -- the audit row is written by the engine (caller of the Lua executor), not by src/lua/ itself. Find: (1) exactly where ScriptResult is produced and consumed in src/engine/ -- trace the call site that invokes the Lua executor and currently discards or ignores manifest_hash; (2) the audit-record schema/write path that currently persists script-execution audit rows -- does the audit table already have a column for this, or does it need a migration? (3) confirm your understanding of the design constraint in src/design/lua-capability-enforcement.md section 11's follow-up note (read that section directly, don't just take the issue's paraphrase). This is a real design decision (which audit write path, whether a schema migration is needed) -- do NOT implement directly, route to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 2) with your findings.
acceptance_criteria: Exact engine call site consuming ScriptResult identified
Current audit-record write path and schema identified -- migration need determined
src/design/lua-capability-enforcement.md section 11 follow-up read directly and its constraints confirmed
Findings routed to CODE-DESIGNER (Step 2), not implemented directly

result.summary: Diagnosis confirms this is a genuine scope-boundary gap, not a defect. (1) src/design/lua-capability-enforcement.md section 6.4 states: 'Rendering that hash into the persisted audit record is the caller's responsibility -- src/lua/ returns the value, the engine writes the row... The corresponding audit-record write is in scope for whichever run owns the engine-side integration; this design commits src/lua/ to producing the value and to nothing else.' Section 11 item 2 restates this as an explicitly deliberate follow-up: 'This design commits src/lua/ to producing the hash on ScriptResult. The engine-side write into the audit row belongs to the engine-integration run; LUA-07's second criterion is only end-to-end satisfied when that lands.' (2) Engine call site: there is currently NO call site at all. `grep -rn "ScriptResult\|executeScript" src/engine/` returns zero matches -- neither transition.zig nor instance.zig references the Lua executor, ScriptResult, or any script/SERVICE_TASK-with-script concept. src/design/lua-integration.md section 6 (Execution Model) still lists script invocation only as a future-stage trigger ('SERVICE_TASK with scriptable behavior', roadmap Phase 2/3 in section 25) -- the engine-to-lua wiring itself has not been built yet, so 'nothing in the engine consumes it and writes it to the audit row' is literally true: nothing in the engine consumes ScriptResult at all yet. (3) Audit-record schema: two generic audit tables exist -- audit_entries (migrations/020_obs03_audit_entries.sql, trigger-driven before/after JSONB snapshots on business tables: process_definitions, instance_projections, tasks, users, groups, group_members, api_tokens, dead_letter_queue) and audit_log (migrations/009_audit_log.sql, append-only with actor/action/entity/detail JSONB columns). Neither has a manifest_hash column or any script-execution-specific shape, and neither is currently populated by any Lua/script code path. A schema migration IS needed once the engine-side integration exists -- either a new column on one of these generic tables, a new script-execution-specific audit table, or use of audit_log's existing flexible `detail JSONB` column (a design decision, not diagnosed here). CONCLUSION: this is exactly the scope-boundary gap the design doc itself documents and defers; the fix requires (a) a design decision on where/how the engine invokes executeScriptWithManifest and (b) a design decision on the audit write path/schema -- both belong to CODE-DESIGNER, not to further diagnosis.
